headline: Consumer credit grew at a 4.2 percent annual rate in July; manufacturers reported higher second-quarter profits

items.title: Consumer Credit (G.19), July 2026
items.summary: The Federal Reserve Board reported that consumer credit increased at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.2 percent in July. Revolving credit grew at an annual rate of 2.5 percent and nonrevolving credit at an annual rate of 4.8 percent. Seasonally adjusted consumer credit outstanding totaled $5,186.2 billion at the end of July; the July figures are marked preliminary.
items.meaning: An annual rate scales one month of growth up to a full year, so 4.2 percent describes the pace in July, not how much consumer credit grew within the month. The release reports revolving and nonrevolving credit separately because they are different kinds of borrowing.

items.title: Quarterly Financial Report: manufacturing, mining, wholesale trade and selected services, second quarter 2026
items.summary: The Census Bureau reported that U.S. manufacturing corporations earned seasonally adjusted after-tax profits of $359.4 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up $64.1 billion from $295.2 billion in the first quarter and up $143.8 billion from $215.6 billion in the second quarter of 2025. Their seasonally adjusted sales totaled $2,324.1 billion, compared with $2,130.1 billion in the first quarter.
items.meaning: These are survey estimates of corporate income statements, so each change is printed with a margin of error: the quarterly rise in manufacturing profits is $64.1 billion plus or minus $1.2 billion.

source.documentTitle: Quarterly Financial Report: U.S. Manufacturing, Mining, Wholesale Trade, and Selected Service Industries, Second Quarter 2026 (CB26-144)

items.title: Quarterly Financial Report: large retail trade corporations, second quarter 2026
items.summary: In a companion release, the Census Bureau reported seasonally adjusted after-tax profits of $112.3 billion for U.S. retail corporations with assets of $50 million and over in the second quarter of 2026, up from $67.2 billion in the first quarter and $60.6 billion in the second quarter of 2025. Their seasonally adjusted sales totaled $1,171.1 billion.
items.meaning: The retail report covers only corporations above an asset threshold of $50 million, so it describes large retailers rather than every store in the country.

sections.title: One concept to know
sections.text: Consumer credit comes in two forms that behave differently. Revolving credit, such as a credit card balance, can be borrowed, repaid, and borrowed again. Nonrevolving credit, such as an auto or student loan, is borrowed once and paid down on a schedule. The Federal Reserve's G.19 release reports the two separately: in July, revolving credit grew at a 2.5 percent annual rate and nonrevolving credit at 4.8 percent.
